subject: Biotechnology
title: Recombinant Growth Hormone
description: A quick, practical guide to Recombinant Growth Hormone.

hook.text: Growth hormone was once harvested from cadaver pituitary glands — some batches transmitted fatal brain disease.

buildup.text: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease from contaminated hormone killed over 200 children — the supply had to change.

discovery.text: Recombinant human growth hormone replaced cadaver sources in 1985 — E. coli produced unlimited, safe supply.

twist.text: Safe supply led to broader use — now prescribed for Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease, and adult deficiency.

climax.text: The transition from cadaver to recombinant happened in just three years — biotech solved a deadly safety crisis.

punchline.text: From cadavers to bacteria — recombinant tech ended a tragedy.

quiz.question: Why was cadaver-derived growth hormone replaced?
options: It was too expensive to extract from pituitary glands
Some batches transmitted Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a fatal brain disorder
It caused allergic reactions in all patients
